scopeMarkdown:
Make RayX.Dtcg a versioned library released **by git tag**: both crates at **1.0.0**, one tag `vX.Y.Z`, one root `CHANGELOG.md` and one GitHub Release per version, cut by release-plz in git-only mode from Conventional Commits. This is the **pilot of the library release template** (RayX.Reactive, RayX.SignalR and Gpux follow it), so the configuration, proofs and docs stay generic where they can.

## In scope

- `release-plz.toml`: git-only, no publish, tag `v{{ version }}`, GitHub Release by release-plz, a release on `feat`/`fix`/`perf` only, `dtcg_runtime_derive` folded into `dtcg_runtime`'s tag, release and root changelog through one version group, RayX.CLI's changelog template plus a line for each `Migration:` footer, `semver_check = false` (1.x policy).
- Version `1.0.0` in `[workspace.package]` and in the workspace's own `[workspace.dependencies]` requirements; `Cargo.lock`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: the configured header; the hand-written `[Unreleased]` content becomes `## [1.0.0] - <release date>`.
- A local release preview with the tool versions `release-plz/action@v0.5` installs (release-plz 0.3.172, cargo-semver-checks 0.51) in a scratch copy: first-release dry run, then docs-only, derive-fix, break-describing `feat` with a `Migration:` footer, and API-removal scenarios.
- `docs/releasing.md`; README Installation and chapter 2 in the git-tag form; chapter 14's Releases, layout and Working with RayX; `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` Releases and Consumers sections.
- `.github/workflows/release-plz.yml` and the first release `v1.0.0` in an owner-dependent final sprint, proven from a scratch consumer outside the repository.

## Amendment 1 (owner, 2026-10-18, later the same day)

- **A. Stay on 1.x.** The owner is the only consumer. Commits are never marked breaking (no `!`, no `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer): a breaking change is a `feat` (or a `fix` when it is one) whose body states the break, with a `Migration:` footer the changelog prints. `semver_check = false`; `release_commits = "^(feat|fix|perf)"`. Before merging a release PR, its proposed version must still be `1.x`; a `2.0.0` proposal means a stray `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:`, and that commit is reworded (force push allowed) instead of merging. The policy ends when a second consumer appears.
- **B.** `ci.yml` keeps its push trigger (as planned); light CI on pushes is fine, release PRs still start nothing heavy.
- **C.** `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` (repository secret, set 2026-10-18T21:09:25Z) and the tag ruleset "Release tags" (`refs/tags/v*`; `update`, `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`; no bypass) exist, verified read-only during the amendment; the epic only verifies them.
- **D.** The owner pre-approved the first-release push and every release-PR merge; the checks before them stay.

## Out of scope

- Publishing to crates.io (manifests stay crates.io-ready; `cargo package --workspace` keeps passing).
- Any change under `crates/`: no API or behaviour change; versions are inherited from the workspace.
- Changing `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (CI-1).
- RayX's switch to the tag (its own epic `rayx-released-libraries`), local override mechanisms (`[patch]` files, `rayx dev link`), Renovate, Dependabot or any GitHub App.
- Promoting this epic's decisions into `.agentx/memory/` (after the epic completes, not a task).

## Deviations from the shared brief (found in the source)

- The README already has `## Installation` with an **unpinned** `git` dependency ("not on crates.io yet"), and chapter 2 (`docs/02-getting-started.md`, "Add the dependency") has the same form; both are reworked (the brief only named a README section to add).
- Chapter 14 has a `## Releases` section about the **crates.io publish order** and a hand-written changelog, and its "Working with RayX" plus `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` "Consumers" describe the `../RayX.Dtcg` path with paired commits; both are rewritten to the release-tag model (owner decision 6).
- `ci.yml` runs on `pull_request` **and on `push` to `main`** (RayX.CLI's is pull-request only). The brief's "release-plz.yml is the only workflow on pushes to the default branch" does not carry over (amendment 1 B confirms): under the push-straight-to-main policy `ci.yml`'s push trigger is the only CI implementation commits get, so it stays and `ci.yml` is not changed at all (CI-1).
- A current repository decision (docs as doctests, 2026-10-07) requires every behaviour change to hand-edit `CHANGELOG.md` with a per-consumer **Migration** subsection. That conflicts with generated changelogs; this epic supersedes its changelog half: migrations move into a `Migration:` footer on the commit, which the template prints from `commit.footers` (an addition to the CLI template).
- The existing changelog header carries a 0.x note and an `## [Unreleased]` heading. release-plz keeps an existing header **verbatim** and inserts new releases right after it (below an Unreleased heading), so the version commit must replace the header with the configured text and drop the Unreleased heading.
- `semver_check`: the brief asked to prove it in git-only mode; amendment 1 turns it off. release-plz's source tests do cover git-only semver checks, and they would only ever check `dtcg_runtime` (proc-macro crates are skipped). The preview now proves the opposite: with cargo-semver-checks installed as in CI, an API removal stays on 1.x (RPZ-4).
- First release order: `release-plz.yml` lands in the final sprint, one push **after** the 1.0.0 commits (which are pushed and CI-checked first); the changelog date is the release push's day (the brief said the version commit's push day).

## Assumptions

- The owner's account `dXnSix` keeps its bypass on the existing branch ruleset `DefaultRules` (default branch: deletion and non-fast-forward blocked), which the force-with-lease push policy relies on.
- `release-plz/action@v0.5` keeps installing release-plz 0.3.172 and cargo-semver-checks 0.51 until the release (checked 2026-10-18); a newer default is re-proven with the preview.
- The token is the PAT RayX.CLI uses, created for "only RayX.CLI"; if its repository access was not extended to RayX.Dtcg, the first Release-plz run fails at checkout or push, and t09 reports that to the owner (fix: add the repository to the PAT) instead of retrying.
- RayX keeps building against `../RayX.Dtcg` until its own epic: its path dependency has no version requirement, so the bump to 1.0.0 only rewrites RayX's `Cargo.lock` on its next build (RayX CI does not use `--locked`).
constraintsMarkdown:
### Owner decisions (2026-10-18), binding

1. Git tags, not crates.io: manifests stay crates.io-ready, nothing is published to a registry.
2. Consumers pin `{ git = "https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.Dtcg", tag = "vX.Y.Z" }`; `Cargo.lock` records the commit; a `v*` tag ruleset blocks moving or deleting tags.
3. Every library starts at **1.0.0** and **stays on 1.x** (amendment 1 A): `fix`/`perf` → patch, `feat` → minor; a breaking change is committed as `feat` (or `fix`) with the break in the body and a `Migration:` footer; never `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:`; `semver_check = false`. The policy ends when a second consumer appears (then `!` and major bumps return).
4. One shared fine-grained PAT as the Actions secret `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN`: it exists as a repository secret here (amendment 1 C); the agent only verifies the secret's name and never creates, reads or handles its value. The `v*` tag ruleset "Release tags" exists too: verify, never create or change it.
5. No local-override mechanism for simultaneous library and RayX edits: release the library first, then RayX bumps its tag by hand. Nothing is planned for it.
6. No Renovate, Dependabot changes or GitHub Apps.

### Push / PR / validation policy (owner, 2026-10-18)

- Implement and test **locally** with focused checks only: no lanes, platform matrices or extra CI runs to close the epic.
- Push straight to `main`, always as `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`, then `git push --force-with-lease origin main` (never drops a merged release PR or a tagged commit). No feature branches, no pull requests for implementation work. Push s1 and s2 after their checkpoints; s3's push is the release itself (FIRST-1).
- Pull requests are used only for releases (release-plz's release PR). The owner pre-approved the first-release push and every release-PR merge (amendment 1 D); their checks stay: light CI green where it runs, the proposed version still `1.x`, the release PR changing only `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `CHANGELOG.md`. Changing GitHub settings (secrets, rulesets) and any by-hand tag still need the owner.
- `release-plz.yml` must land in the same push as or after the `1.0.0` version, never before (it would tag `0.1.0`); here it lands after (d-release-workflow).

### Repository rules

- Conventional Commits with meaningful scopes; never add Claude co-author lines. Suggested types: `build(release)` for release configuration, `chore(release)` for the version commit, `docs(...)` for docs, `ci(release)` for the workflow. Never `!` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer (1.x policy).
- Nothing under `crates/` changes (forbidden path): versions are inherited; the derive crate's dev-dependency on `dtcg_runtime` stays path-only (packaging rule).
- README and every `docs/` file keep a language tag on every code block; README and the guide chapters stay doctests (`cargo test -p dtcg_runtime --all-features --doc documentation::<chapter>`).
- `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` stay byte-identical, AgentX block included.
- HARD RULE: test only what changed. The sprint checks are this epic's own static checks and the doctests of the touched pages; no workspace test suite, no corpus run, no wasm build. The final check is `cargo package --workspace` (manifest change).
- Scratch work (the release preview copy, the tag consumer) happens in system temporary directories, never in the repository; raw logs belong in ignored `artifacts-temp/agentx/dtcg-releases/`. Never run a preview scenario's commands (`git tag`, commits, `release-plz update`) in the repository itself.
- Tools for the local proof: release-plz 0.3.172 and cargo-semver-checks 0.51.x (installed so the preview proves that `semver_check = false` really keeps an API removal on 1.x, as CI has it installed) installed with `cargo install --locked` from crates.io into the user's cargo bin (not committed). `python3` may be 3.9 (macOS): the checks fall back to pip's vendored `tomli` when `tomllib` is missing.

requirements.title: release-plz configuration and its proven behaviour
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: One release unit per repository version: `dtcg_runtime` owns the tag, the GitHub Release and the root changelog; `dtcg_runtime_derive` follows its version. Proven locally with the release tooling CI uses, under the 1.x policy (amendment 1 A).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`release-plz.toml` at the repository root:

- `[workspace]`: `git_only = true`, `publish = false`, `git_tag_enable = true`, `git_tag_name = "v{{ version }}"`, `git_release_enable = true`, `changelog_update = true`, `semver_check = false` and `release_commits = "^(feat|fix|perf)"` (amendment 1 A), so `docs:`, `refactor(x):`, `build:`, `chore(agentx):` alone do not release.
- `[[package]] dtcg_runtime`: `changelog_path = "./CHANGELOG.md"`, `changelog_include = ["dtcg_runtime_derive"]`, `version_group = "dtcg"`; tag, release and changelog stay on.
- `[[package]] dtcg_runtime_derive`: the same `version_group`, `git_tag_enable = false`, `git_release_enable = false`, `changelog_update = false`; it inherits `git_tag_name` (git-only mode finds its previous version through that template) and is not `release = false`.
- `[changelog]`: RayX.CLI's template (Keep a Changelog header naming both crates and release-plz, without an `## [Unreleased]` heading; `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` body with groups; `trim`, `protect_breaking_commits`, `tag_pattern = "v[0-9].*"`, `sort_commits = "oldest"`; skip `chore(agentx)`, `chore(release)`, `chore(deps)`), plus, for each `Migration:` footer of a commit, an indented `Migration: <value>` line under the entry (git-cliff's `commit.footers`, token `Migration`).
- Comments say why git-only, why one version group, and the 1.x policy (why `semver_check` is off and `!` is not used: release-plz cannot cap a major bump).

Verified by `check-release-config`.

First release without a pull request: with `1.0.0` in the manifests and no `v*` tag, `release-plz release --dry-run` (scratch copy, placeholder token, nothing pushed) plans the tag `v1.0.0` and a GitHub Release for `dtcg_runtime`, and nothing for `dtcg_runtime_derive` ("no release method enabled", no `dtcg_runtime_derive-v*` tag). Verified by `check-release-preview`.

No automatic major (1.x policy): `semver_check = false`, and in the preview, with cargo-semver-checks 0.51 on PATH (CI has it installed, so its mere presence must not matter), a `fix(dtcg_runtime): …` commit that removes a public function present at `v1.0.0` makes `release-plz update` propose `1.0.1`, and no API check runs (no "Checking API compatibility" or "API breaking changes" in its log). Verified by `check-release-preview`.

requirements.title: Version 1.0.0 and the first changelog section
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: A clean start at 1.0.0 that keeps the hand-written history as the 1.0.0 notes.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown: `[workspace.package] version = "1.0.0"`; the `[workspace.dependencies]` entries `dtcg_runtime` and `dtcg_runtime_derive` keep their `path` and say `version = "1.0.0"`; `Cargo.lock` records both crates at `1.0.0`; the derive crate's dev-dependency stays `{ path = "../dtcg_runtime" }`; nothing under `crates/` changes. Verified by `check-version-changelog`; `cargo package --workspace` (final check) still passes.

`CHANGELOG.md` starts with exactly the `[changelog] header` of `release-plz.toml` (no 0.x note, no `## [Unreleased]` heading), followed by its only `##` heading `## [1.0.0] - YYYY-MM-DD`, whose body is the former `[Unreleased]` content of commit `7d55b99`, unchanged (intro, Added, Changed, Fixed, and the Migration subsections for RayX and RayX.TokenEditor). The date is the day of the push that releases `v1.0.0` (set when written, corrected in s3 if the release push happens on a later day). Verified by `check-version-changelog`.

requirements.title: Release documentation, install by tag and contributor guidance
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Maintainers know how a release happens and what can go wrong; consumers depend only on release tags; agents follow the commit, release and push rules.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown: README `## Installation`: releases are git tags, not crates.io; depend on `dtcg_runtime = { git = "https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.Dtcg", tag = "v1.0.0" }`; take the latest tag from the repository's Releases page; `Cargo.lock` records the exact commit; a library is consumed only by release tag (never by branch or path). The existing notes (optional `serde_json`, derive macros re-exported, the `diagnostics` feature) stay. Chapter 2's "Add the dependency" uses the same tag form. No unpinned `git = "https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.Dtcg" }` and no "not on crates.io yet" remain in README or chapter 2. Both stay passing doctests (`toml` blocks). Verified by `check-release-docs` and `check-doc-doctests`.

Chapter 14 (`docs/14-architecture-and-contributing.md`): `## Releases` summarises the release-plz flow (one version, tag and changelog for both crates; Conventional Commits; release PR; git tags only) and links `docs/releasing.md`, with no crates.io publish order, crates.io-readme note or hand-written changelog rule; the source-layout tree lists `release-plz.toml`, `.github/workflows/release-plz.yml` and `docs/releasing.md`; `## Working with RayX` says RayX depends on a release tag and that a change RayX needs is released here first, then RayX bumps its tag by hand and validates (no relative path, no paired commits). `## CI` stays accurate. Verified by `check-release-docs` and `check-doc-doctests`.

`CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` stay identical (AgentX block included) and gain a short `## Releases` section: Conventional Commits drive the version; the 1.x policy (never `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:`; a breaking change is a `feat` or `fix` whose body states the break, with a `Migration:` footer per consumer; ends when a second consumer appears); `CHANGELOG.md` is written by release-plz; a release is the merge of release-plz's release pull request after checking that it proposes a `1.x` version and changes only `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `CHANGELOG.md`; the push policy (`git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`, then `git push --force-with-lease origin main`; no feature branches or pull requests except release PRs); a link to `docs/releasing.md`. Their `## Consumers` section names the tag form and the release-first rule instead of the relative path and paired commits. Verified by `check-agent-guidance`.

requirements.title: Release PR CI stays cheap
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: A release PR changes only `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `CHANGELOG.md`; it must not start heavy suites.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown: A release PR (head branch `release-plz-*`) starts only `ci.yml`: one job on `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest` running `cargo fmt --check`, clippy, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` check and `cargo package --workspace` (2.5 to 4 minutes per recent run, 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-07). No e2e, performance, lane or larger matrix suites exist, so `ci.yml` stays byte-identical to `7d55b99` (forbidden path), including its `push: main` trigger. `docs/releasing.md` states what a release PR runs. The reviewer confirms with `git diff 7d55b99 -- .github/workflows/ci.yml` (empty) and the documented statement.

requirements.title: The release-plz workflow
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: RayX.CLI's release-plz workflow, adapted to this repository and to release-plz creating the GitHub Release.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown: `.github/workflows/release-plz.yml`: name `Release-plz`; on `push` to `main` and `workflow_dispatch` only; jobs `release` (`contents: write`) and `release-pr` (`contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`, `needs: release`, so on every push, above all the first one whose untagged history still holds `feat!` commits, the release PR is computed only after `release` has tagged), each guarded by `github.repository == 'rayx-ui/RayX.Dtcg'`, on `ubuntu-24.04`, with its own non-cancelling concurrency group; steps `actions/checkout` (the major `ci.yml` uses) with `fetch-depth: 0` and `token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN }}`, `actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain@v1` (`cache: false`, `rustflags: ""`; reads `rust-toolchain.toml`), and `release-plz/action@v0.5` with `command: release` / `release-pr` and `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN }}`. `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` is the only secret; no test, build, check or clippy steps. The header comment explains the two jobs, the token, that release-plz (not dist) creates the GitHub Release, and that `ci.yml` (pull requests and pushes) does the testing. Verified by `check-workflow-yaml` and `check-release-workflow`; pushed only as FIRST-1 describes.

requirements.title: Owner prerequisites, verified
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: GitHub-side setup the owner completed on 2026-10-18 (amendment 1 C); the epic only verifies it, read-only.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown: The repository secret `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` exists (set 2026-10-18T21:09:25Z; the PAT RayX.CLI uses). Verified by `check-release-secret`, which reads secret names only; the agent never sees or handles the value. Whether the PAT's repository access includes RayX.Dtcg is proven only by FIRST-1's run passing checkout and the tag push.

The owner's tag ruleset "Release tags" is active, includes `refs/tags/v*`, restricts updates and deletions (it also has `non_fast_forward`; creation stays allowed for release-plz) and has no bypass actors. Verify only; never create or change it. Verified by `check-tag-ruleset`.

requirements.title: The first release v1.0.0
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Owner-dependent acceptance on GitHub, then proof that consumers can use the tag.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown: With OWN-1 and OWN-2 verified and `ci.yml` green on `main` for the pushed s1 and s2 commits (the owner pre-approved this push, amendment 1 D), the push that adds `release-plz.yml` (and, if the day changed, the corrected `1.0.0` date) runs Release-plz on `main`: the `release` job tags `v1.0.0` on that push and creates the GitHub Release `v1.0.0` (not draft, not prerelease) whose notes are the `1.0.0` changelog section; no per-crate tag exists; `release-pr` opens no release pull request; the latest Release-plz run on `main` succeeded; `Cargo.toml` at `v1.0.0` says `1.0.0`. Verified by `check-first-release`. If the run fails at checkout or the tag push (the PAT's repository access), the implementer reports it to the owner (fix: add RayX.Dtcg to the PAT) instead of retrying blindly; the by-hand fallback is used only with the owner's go-ahead, with the reason recorded as a finding.

A scratch Cargo package created outside the repository (system temp directory, toolchain 1.95.0) with `dtcg_runtime = { git = "https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.Dtcg", tag = "v1.0.0" }` resolves and builds (`cargo check`), and `cargo tree` shows `dtcg_runtime v1.0.0` and `dtcg_runtime_derive v1.0.0` both from `https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.Dtcg?tag=v1.0.0#<commit>`. Verified by `check-tag-consumer`.
